records.literal_gloss: [Is there] not hard service for humankind on earth, and like [the] days of a hired laborer [are] his days?

en.L: [Is there] not hard service for {{gender:mortals|man}} on earth, \q and like [the] days of a hired laborer [are] not {{gender:their|his}} days?
en.B: {{gender:Do not mortals have|Does not man have}} hard service on earth, \q and are {{gender:their|his}} days not like the days of a hired worker?
en.R: Every human being has hard service to do on earth; \q their days are like the days of a worker hired for pay.

es.L: ¿No [hay] dura milicia para {{gender:el mortal|el hombre}} sobre la tierra, \q y no [son] sus días como [los] días de un jornalero?
es.B: ¿No tiene {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} un duro servicio sobre la tierra, \q y no son sus días como los de un jornalero?
es.R: Todo ser humano tiene un duro servicio que cumplir en la tierra; \q sus días son como los de un trabajador a sueldo.

fr.L: N’[y a-t-il] pas un dur service pour {{gender:le mortel|l’homme}} sur la terre, \q et ses jours ne [sont-ils] pas comme [les] jours d’un ouvrier salarié ?
fr.B: {{gender:L’être humain n’a-t-il|L’homme n’a-t-il}} pas un dur service sur la terre, \q et ses jours ne sont-ils pas comme ceux d’un ouvrier à gages ?
fr.R: Tout être humain a un dur service à accomplir sur la terre ; \q ses jours sont comme ceux d’un ouvrier payé à la journée.

sw.L: Je, [hakuna] utumishi mgumu kwa mwanadamu duniani, \q na siku zake [si] kama siku za kibarua?
sw.B: Je, mwanadamu hana utumishi mgumu duniani, \q na siku zake si kama siku za mfanyakazi wa kuajiriwa?
sw.R: Kila mwanadamu ana utumishi mgumu wa kufanya duniani; \q siku zake ni kama siku za kibarua anayelipwa ujira.

vi.L: Há chẳng [có] sự lao dịch nặng nhọc cho loài người trên đất, \q và ngày của họ chẳng [như] ngày của người làm thuê sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải con người phải lao dịch nặng nhọc trên đất, \q và chuỗi ngày của họ như ngày của người làm công sao?
vi.R: Ai sống trên đất cũng phải làm lụng vất vả; \q đời họ như những ngày của người làm thuê lãnh công.

ko.L: 땅 위에 있는 사람에게 고된 복무가 [있지] 않은가? \q 그의 날들이 품꾼의 날들과 같지 않은가?
ko.B: 사람은 땅에서 고된 복무를 하고 있지 않은가? \q 그 날들이 품꾼의 날들과 같지 않은가?
ko.R: 모든 사람은 땅에서 고된 일을 해야 한다. \q 그들의 날은 삯을 받고 일하는 품꾼의 날과 같다.

decisions.choice: hard service: a fixed term of hard, compulsory duty
decisions.reason: The word (tsava') usually means an army or military service. Here, as in Isaiah 40:2, it is a set term of hard duty that a person cannot leave until it is over. Job uses it of his own life again in 14:14 ("all the days of my service").

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question begins with the Hebrew question marker and "not": "Is it not so ...?" Job is stating something he takes as plain to everyone. The second half shares the question.

decisions.choice: a hired laborer: a worker paid by the day
decisions.reason: A hired laborer (sakhir) worked for a wage paid at the end of each day (Leviticus 19:13; Deuteronomy 24:14-15). His days were hard, counted, and not his own. The next verse takes up the picture.

decisions.choice: humankind: any mortal, not a male only
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) means a human being, often with a sense of frailty (7:17). Job speaks of the lot of everyone, himself included.

decisions.choice: mortals ... their (L), with "man ... his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The words are singular and masculine but mean anyone (m4), so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
alternatives: Is not human life hard service?
decisions.reason: The question expects yes (m2), so Readable states it plainly. The meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: plain 해라체 for descriptive, proverbial and self-lamenting lines inside a speech; 하오체 with 그대/그대들 only where the speaker addresses his listener; Job's lament in 7:1-6 is plain style, and from 7:7 he speaks to God in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: A whole poem in 하오체 makes general sayings sound like remarks to one person; Korean keeps the polite address for direct address, questions, commands and "you" statements, and states the rest in the plain written style, with -시- for God (coordinator's ruling for Job).

source.text: כְּעֶ֥בֶד יִשְׁאַף־צֵ֑ל וּ֝כְשָׂכִ֗יר יְקַוֶּ֥ה פָעֳלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a slave [who] pants for shade, and like a hired laborer [who] waits for his wages,

en.L: Like a slave [who] longs for [the] shade, \q and like a hired laborer [who] waits for his wages,
en.B: Like a slave who longs for the shade, \q and like a hired worker who waits for his pay,
en.R: Like a slave who longs for the cool evening shade, \q like a worker waiting to be paid,

es.L: Como un esclavo [que] anhela [la] sombra, \q y como un jornalero [que] espera su salario,
es.B: Como el esclavo que suspira por la sombra, \q y como el jornalero que espera su paga,
es.R: Como un esclavo que desea la sombra fresca de la tarde, \q como un trabajador que espera su paga,

fr.L: Comme un esclave [qui] soupire après l’ombre, \q et comme un ouvrier salarié [qui] attend son salaire,
fr.B: Comme l’esclave qui soupire après l’ombre, \q comme l’ouvrier à gages qui attend sa paie,
fr.R: Comme un esclave qui attend avec impatience l’ombre fraîche du soir, \q comme un ouvrier qui attend d’être payé,

sw.L: Kama mtumwa anayetamani kivuli, \q na kama kibarua anayengojea ujira wake,
sw.B: Kama mtumwa anayetamani kivuli, \q na kama kibarua anayesubiri malipo yake,
sw.R: Kama mtumwa anayetamani kivuli cha jioni chenye baridi, \q kama mfanyakazi anayesubiri kulipwa,

vi.L: Như nô lệ thèm khát bóng râm, \q và như người làm thuê trông chờ tiền công mình,
vi.B: Như người nô lệ mong bóng chiều, \q như người làm công chờ đợi tiền lương,
vi.R: Như người nô lệ mong bóng mát buổi chiều, \q như người làm thuê chờ được trả công,

ko.L: 그늘을 갈망하는 노예처럼, \q 자기 삯을 기다리는 품꾼처럼,
ko.B: 그늘을 애타게 바라는 노예처럼, \q 품삯을 기다리는 품꾼처럼,
ko.R: 선선한 저녁 그늘을 기다리는 노예처럼, \q 품삯 받기를 기다리는 일꾼처럼,

decisions.choice: slave: a laborer owned by a master, set against one who is hired
decisions.reason: The word ('eved) here is set beside the hired laborer: one is owned and works without wages, the other is paid by the day. Both long for the day's work to end.

decisions.choice: the shade: the shadows of evening, when work stops
decisions.reason: The worker in the field longs for the shade, the lengthening shadows of evening (Jeremiah 6:4) that end the working day. It may also be shade from the sun's heat; either way it is relief he waits for.

decisions.choice: the comparison runs on into verse 3
decisions.reason: The two "like" clauses are completed by "so" at the start of verse 3: as the slave and the laborer wait, so Job has been given empty months.

decisions.choice: slave, at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "slave" where slavery itself is the point. Here the owned slave is set against the hired worker (m1), so "servant" would lose the contrast.

decisions.choice: the cool evening shade
decisions.reason: Readable says what the shade means for the worker (m2): the cool of evening, when work ends.

decisions.choice: "노예" rather than "종"
decisions.reason: The owned slave is set against the hired worker (m1), so Korean uses the word for slavery itself; "종" would blur the contrast with "품꾼".

source.text: כֵּ֤ן הָנְחַ֣לְתִּי לִ֭י יַרְחֵי־שָׁ֑וְא וְלֵיל֥וֹת עָ֝מָ֗ל מִנּוּ־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: So I have been allotted for myself months of emptiness, and nights of trouble they have appointed to me.

en.L: so I have been allotted months of emptiness, \q and nights of misery they have counted out to me.
en.B: so I have been given months of emptiness as my share, \q and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
en.R: so I have been handed months that come to nothing, \q and nights full of misery have been measured out to me.

es.L: así me han tocado en herencia meses de vacío, \q y noches de miseria me han asignado.
es.B: así he recibido como herencia meses de vacío, \q y se me han asignado noches de miseria.
es.R: así me han dado meses que no llevan a nada, \q y me han medido noches llenas de sufrimiento.

fr.L: ainsi j’ai reçu en partage des mois de vide, \q et des nuits de misère, on me les a comptées.
fr.B: ainsi j’ai reçu pour ma part des mois de néant, \q et des nuits de misère m’ont été assignées.
fr.R: ainsi on m’a donné des mois qui ne mènent à rien, \q et des nuits pleines de misère m’ont été mesurées.

sw.L: ndivyo nilivyopewa urithi wa miezi ya ubatili, \q na usiku wa taabu wamenigawia.
sw.B: ndivyo nilivyopewa miezi ya ubatili kuwa fungu langu, \q na nimepangiwa usiku wa taabu.
sw.R: ndivyo nilivyopewa miezi isiyo na faida yoyote, \q na nimepimiwa usiku uliojaa mateso.

vi.L: thì tôi cũng được chia phần những tháng hư không, \q và những đêm khốn khổ người ta đã định cho tôi.
vi.B: thì tôi cũng nhận phần những tháng ngày vô ích, \q và những đêm khổ sở đã được định sẵn cho tôi.
vi.R: thì tôi cũng bị trao cho những tháng ngày chẳng đi đến đâu, \q và những đêm đầy khốn khổ đã được đong cho tôi.

ko.L: 나도 헛된 달들을 유산으로 받았고, \q 괴로운 밤들을 그들이 내게 정해 주었다.
ko.B: 나도 허무한 달들을 내 몫으로 받았고, \q 괴로운 밤들이 내게 정해졌다.
ko.R: 나도 아무 보람 없는 달들을 받았고, \q 괴로움으로 가득한 밤들이 내게 할당되었다.

decisions.choice: allotted: given as one's inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb (nachal) is used for receiving land as an inheritance (Numbers 34:13). Job speaks bitterly: his share, his inheritance, is months of emptiness.

decisions.choice: emptiness: months that come to nothing
decisions.reason: The word (shav') means what is empty, worthless or false. The months are wasted, without any good in them.

decisions.choice: they have appointed: an impersonal plural, equal to a passive
decisions.reason: Hebrew often uses "they" with no named subject to mean a passive: nights have been appointed to Job. Job does not say who gives them; in 7:12-21 he speaks to God as the one behind his suffering.

decisions.choice: misery: trouble and toil
decisions.reason: The word ('amal) means hard toil and the trouble it brings (3:10; 5:6-7). His nights bring no rest.

decisions.choice: have been assigned to me
alternatives: they have counted out to me
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English passive for the impersonal "they" (m3); Literal keeps "they".

source.text: אִם־שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מָתַ֣י אָ֭קוּם וּמִדַּד־עָ֑רֶב וְשָׂבַ֖עְתִּי נְדֻדִ֣ים עֲדֵי־נָֽשֶׁף׃

records.literal_gloss: If I lie down, and I say, When will I rise? And [the] evening stretches out, and I am full of tossings until twilight.

en.L: If I lie down, then I say, "When will I rise?" \q and [the] evening stretches on, \q and I am sated with tossings until [the] dawn.
en.B: When I lie down I think, "When will I get up?" \q But the night drags on, \q and I toss and turn until dawn.
en.R: When I lie down, I think, "How long until I can get up?" \q But the night goes on and on, \q and I toss and turn until morning.

es.L: Si me acuesto, digo: «¿Cuándo me levantaré?», \q y [la] tarde se alarga, \q y me harto de dar vueltas hasta el alba.
es.B: Cuando me acuesto pienso: «¿Cuándo me levantaré?». \q Pero la noche se alarga, \q y doy vueltas y vueltas hasta el amanecer.
es.R: Cuando me acuesto, pienso: «¿Cuánto falta para poder levantarme?». \q Pero la noche sigue y sigue, \q y doy vueltas en la cama hasta la mañana.

fr.L: Si je me couche, je dis : « Quand me lèverai-je ? » \q et le soir se prolonge, \q et je suis rassasié d’agitation jusqu’à [l’]aube.
fr.B: Quand je me couche, je pense : « Quand vais-je me lever ? » \q Mais la nuit n’en finit pas, \q et je me tourne et me retourne jusqu’à l’aube.
fr.R: Quand je me couche, je me dis : « Combien de temps encore avant de pouvoir me lever ? » \q Mais la nuit dure, dure, \q et je me tourne et me retourne jusqu’au matin.

sw.L: Nikilala, nasema, "Nitaamka lini?" \q na jioni inarefuka, \q nami nashibishwa na kugaagaa hadi alfajiri.
sw.B: Ninapolala nawaza, "Nitaamka lini?" \q Lakini usiku unaendelea, \q nami najigeuza-geuza mpaka alfajiri.
sw.R: Ninapolala, nawaza, "Itachukua muda gani mpaka niamke?" \q Lakini usiku unaendelea bila kwisha, \q nami najigeuza-geuza mpaka asubuhi.

vi.L: Nếu tôi nằm xuống, thì tôi nói: "Khi nào tôi sẽ dậy?" \q và buổi tối kéo dài, \q và tôi trằn trọc chán chê cho đến bình minh.
vi.B: Khi nằm xuống tôi nghĩ: "Bao giờ mới được dậy?" \q Nhưng đêm cứ kéo dài, \q và tôi trằn trọc cho đến sáng.
vi.R: Khi nằm xuống, tôi nghĩ: "Còn bao lâu nữa mới được dậy?" \q Nhưng đêm cứ dài mãi, \q và tôi trở mình trằn trọc cho đến sáng.

ko.L: 내가 누우면 "언제 일어날까?" 하고 말하나, \q 저녁은 길어지고, \q 나는 새벽까지 뒤척임에 지친다.
ko.B: 누우면 "언제 일어나나?" 하고 생각하지만, \q 밤은 길기만 하고, \q 나는 새벽까지 뒤척인다.
ko.R: 누우면 "언제나 일어날 수 있을까?" 하고 생각하지만, \q 밤은 끝없이 이어지고, \q 나는 아침까지 이리저리 뒤척인다.

decisions.choice: stretches on: the evening is long
alternatives: When will the evening be over?
decisions.reason: The verb (madad, "measure") is unusual here; with "evening" it seems to mean that the evening is measured out long. Some take it as part of Job's question ("When will the night be measured out?"). The sense is the same: the night will not end.

decisions.choice: twilight: here the dawn
decisions.reason: The word (neshef) means the half-light of either evening or morning (24:15; Psalm 119:147). After a night of tossing it must be the dawn.

decisions.choice: I say: I think to myself
decisions.reason: The verb "say" often means to say in one's heart, to think (Genesis 20:11). Job is lying awake, not speaking aloud.

decisions.choice: tossings: restless turning
decisions.reason: The word (nedudim) comes from a root meaning to wander or flee; here it is the restless turning of a man who cannot sleep. He is "full" of it, had more than enough.

decisions.choice: night
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "evening" ('erev), the time from sunset on. Since Job lies awake until dawn, Balanced and Readable say "night"; Literal keeps "evening".

source.text: לָ֘בַ֤שׁ בְּשָׂרִ֣י רִ֭מָּה וְג֣וּשׁ עָפָ֑ר עוֹרִ֥י רָ֝גַ֗ע וַיִּמָּאֵֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: My flesh is clothed [with] worms and clods of dust; my skin hardens and oozes.

en.L: My flesh is clothed [with] worms and clods of dust; \q my skin hardens, and it oozes.
en.B: My body is covered with worms and crusts of dirt; \q my skin scabs over and then oozes again.
en.R: My body is covered with maggots and crusty scabs like dirt. \q My skin hardens and then runs again.

es.L: Mi carne está vestida de gusanos y de terrones de polvo; \q mi piel se endurece, y supura.
es.B: Mi cuerpo está cubierto de gusanos y de costras de tierra; \q mi piel forma costra y luego vuelve a supurar.
es.R: Mi cuerpo está cubierto de gusanos y de costras como de tierra. \q Mi piel se endurece y luego vuelve a supurar.

fr.L: Ma chair est revêtue de vers et de croûtes de poussière ; \q ma peau durcit, et elle suppure.
fr.B: Mon corps est couvert de vers et de croûtes de terre ; \q ma peau se couvre de croûtes, puis suinte de nouveau.
fr.R: Mon corps est couvert d’asticots et de croûtes comme de la terre. \q Ma peau durcit, puis coule de nouveau.

sw.L: Mwili wangu umevikwa mabuu na mabonge ya mavumbi; \q ngozi yangu inakuwa ngumu, na inatoa usaha.
sw.B: Mwili wangu umefunikwa na mabuu na magamba ya uchafu; \q ngozi yangu inaganda kisha inatoa usaha tena.
sw.R: Mwili wangu umejaa funza na makovu magumu kama udongo. \q Ngozi yangu inakuwa ngumu kisha inatoa usaha tena.

vi.L: Thịt tôi mặc lấy giòi bọ và cục đất bụi; \q da tôi cứng lại, rồi chảy mủ.
vi.B: Thân thể tôi phủ đầy giòi bọ và vảy bẩn như đất; \q da tôi đóng vảy rồi lại chảy mủ.
vi.R: Thân thể tôi đầy giòi và vảy cứng như đất. \q Da tôi khô cứng lại rồi lại chảy nước.

ko.L: 내 살은 구더기와 흙덩이로 옷 입었고, \q 내 피부는 굳었다가 진물이 흐른다.
ko.B: 내 몸은 구더기와 흙 같은 딱지로 덮였고, \q 내 피부는 딱지가 앉았다가 다시 진물이 흐른다.
ko.R: 내 몸은 구더기와 흙덩이 같은 딱지로 뒤덮였다. \q 피부가 굳었다가 다시 진물이 흐른다.

decisions.choice: worms: maggots in the sores
decisions.reason: The word (rimmah) is used of maggots in rotting food (Exodus 16:24) and in the grave (17:14; 21:26). Job's body is covered with the sores of 2:7, and worms breed in them.

decisions.choice: clods of dust: dirty crusts on the skin
alternatives: the dust of the ash heap
decisions.reason: "Clods of dust" may be scabs that look like lumps of earth, or the dirt and ashes Job sits in (2:8) caked on his sores. Either way his skin is crusted and filthy.

decisions.choice: oozes: the sores break and run
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning to melt or flow (as Psalm 58:8) or from a root meaning to reject (as in 7:16). With "hardens" just before it, the sense is that the skin crusts over and then breaks and runs again.

decisions.choice: hardens: crusts over
decisions.reason: The verb (raga') here seems to mean to harden or crust; some take it as "cracks". The line pictures sores that will not heal.

decisions.choice: body
decisions.reason: "Flesh" (basar) here means the body; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "flesh".

source.text: יָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־אָ֑רֶג וַ֝יִּכְל֗וּ בְּאֶ֣פֶס תִּקְוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end with no hope.

en.L: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, \q and they come to an end without hope.
en.B: My days go faster than a weaver's shuttle; \q they come to an end without hope.
en.R: My days fly by faster than a shuttle on a loom, \q and they run out with no hope left.

es.L: Mis días son más veloces que la lanzadera del tejedor, \q y se acaban sin esperanza.
es.B: Mis días corren más que la lanzadera del tejedor; \q llegan a su fin sin esperanza.
es.R: Mis días pasan volando, más rápido que una lanzadera en el telar, \q y se acaban sin que quede esperanza.

fr.L: Mes jours sont plus rapides que la navette du tisserand, \q et ils prennent fin sans espoir.
fr.B: Mes jours vont plus vite que la navette du tisserand ; \q ils s’achèvent sans espoir.
fr.R: Mes jours filent plus vite qu’une navette sur un métier à tisser, \q et ils s’épuisent sans qu’il reste d’espoir.

sw.L: Siku zangu zinakwenda mbio kuliko chombo cha mfumaji, \q nazo zinakwisha bila tumaini.
sw.B: Siku zangu zinapita upesi kuliko chombo cha mfumaji; \q zinakoma bila tumaini.
sw.R: Siku zangu zinapita kasi kuliko chombo cha kufumia kinachopitisha uzi, \q nazo zinakwisha bila tumaini lolote kubaki.

vi.L: Ngày tháng tôi qua nhanh hơn thoi dệt cửi, \q và chúng chấm dứt không còn hy vọng.
vi.B: Ngày tháng tôi trôi nhanh hơn con thoi của thợ dệt; \q chúng tàn đi chẳng còn chút hy vọng.
vi.R: Những ngày của tôi vụt qua nhanh hơn con thoi trên khung cửi, \q và chúng cạn dần, chẳng còn hy vọng gì.

ko.L: 내 날들은 베틀의 북보다 빠르고, \q 소망 없이 끝나 버린다.
ko.B: 내 날들은 베 짜는 사람의 북보다 빨리 지나가고, \q 희망 없이 끝나 간다.
ko.R: 내 날들은 베틀의 북보다 빨리 지나가 버리고, \q 남은 희망 하나 없이 다 끝나 간다.

decisions.choice: a weaver's shuttle: the tool that runs back and forth across the loom
decisions.reason: The word ('ereg) is used for weaving and the loom (Judges 16:14). The shuttle carries the thread quickly across and back, so it is a picture of speed.

decisions.choice: hope, and also "thread"
decisions.reason: The word for hope (tiqwah) is the same as the word for a cord or thread (Joshua 2:18, 21). After the weaver's shuttle, the line can be heard both ways: Job's days end without hope, as a piece of weaving ends when the thread runs out. The text means "hope"; the second sense is a play on words.

decisions.choice: come to an end: are finished
decisions.reason: The verb (kalah) means to be completed or used up. It is used of time running out (Psalm 90:9).

decisions.choice: fly by
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common English phrase for time passing quickly.

source.text: זְ֭כֹר כִּי־ר֣וּחַ חַיָּ֑י לֹא־תָשׁ֥וּב עֵ֝ינִ֗י לִרְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember that my life [is] a breath; my eye will not return to see good.

en.L: Remember that my life [is] a breath; \q my eye will not again see good.
en.B: Remember that my life is only a breath; \q my eyes will never again see anything good.
en.R: God, remember that my life is only a breath. \q I will never again see good times.

es.L: Recuerda que mi vida [es] un soplo; \q mi ojo no volverá a ver el bien.
es.B: Recuerda que mi vida es solo un soplo; \q mis ojos nunca más verán nada bueno.
es.R: Dios, recuerda que mi vida es solo un soplo. \q Nunca más veré tiempos buenos.

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que ma vie [est] un souffle ; \q mon œil ne verra plus le bonheur.
fr.B: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que ma vie n’est qu’un souffle ; \q mes yeux ne verront plus jamais le bonheur.
fr.R: Dieu, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que ma vie n’est qu’un souffle. \q Je ne connaîtrai plus jamais de jours heureux.

sw.L: Kumbuka kwamba maisha yangu [ni] pumzi; \q jicho langu halitaona tena mema.
sw.B: Kumbuka kwamba maisha yangu ni pumzi tu; \q macho yangu hayataona tena jema lolote.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, kumbuka kwamba maisha yangu ni pumzi tu. \q Sitaona tena nyakati njema.

vi.L: Xin Chúa nhớ rằng đời con [chỉ là] một hơi thở; \q mắt con sẽ chẳng còn thấy điều tốt lành.
vi.B: Xin Chúa nhớ rằng đời con chỉ là hơi thở; \q mắt con sẽ chẳng bao giờ thấy lại điều tốt lành.
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, xin nhớ rằng đời con chỉ là một hơi thở. \q Con sẽ không bao giờ được thấy những ngày tốt đẹp nữa.

ko.L: 제 생명이 숨결임을 기억하십시오. \q 제 눈이 다시 좋은 것을 보지 못할 것입니다.
ko.B: 제 생명이 한낱 숨결에 지나지 않음을 기억해 주십시오. \q 제 눈은 다시는 좋은 것을 보지 못할 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님, 제 목숨이 한 번의 숨결과 같다는 것을 기억해 주십시오. \q 저는 다시는 좋은 날을 보지 못할 것입니다.

decisions.choice: Job now speaks to God
decisions.reason: The verb "remember" is an imperative addressed to one person, and from here to the end of the chapter Job speaks to God directly: "your eyes" (7:8), "you set a guard over me" (7:12), "watcher of humankind" (7:20).

decisions.choice: a breath: something brief and without substance
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) means wind or breath. As in Psalm 78:39 ("a breath that passes and does not return"), it pictures a life that is soon gone.

decisions.choice: see good: enjoy any good thing
decisions.reason: To "see good" is to experience good, to enjoy life (Ecclesiastes 2:24; Psalm 34:13). "Will not return to see" is the Hebrew way of saying "will never again see".

decisions.choice: God, remember
decisions.reason: Readable names God, because the change of addressee (m1) is not marked in English and a reader could think Job is still speaking to his friends.

decisions.choice: "souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}": the imperative’s pronoun takes the span
decisions.reason: French imperatives carry a pronoun where English has none, and the book's terms note spans it when God is addressed (as 2 Kings 20:3), so the capitalised option reads "Souviens-Toi".

decisions.choice: Job, now speaking to God, calls him "Chúa" and himself "con" (not "tôi" as with his friends)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must name the relation in every pronoun; the terms note gives Job's prayers the psalmists' "Chúa" / "con". His words here are bitter, and "tôi" would keep more of their edge, so a reviewer should weigh it.

decisions.choice: Job turns from the plain style of his lament to 합쇼체 with "주님" and "저" to God (기억하십시오, 못할 것입니다)
decisions.reason: The change of speech level shows the change of addressee (m1), as the Psalms' laments do; it holds to the end of the chapter.

source.text: לֹֽא־תְ֭שׁוּרֵנִי עֵ֣ין רֹ֑אִי עֵינֶ֖יךָ בִּ֣י וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will see me [the] eye of one seeing [me]; your eyes [are] on me, and I [am] not.

en.L: The eye of [the one who] sees me will not see me [again]; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes [will be] on me, but I [will be] no more.
en.B: The eye that sees me now will see me no more; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes will look for me, but I will be gone.
en.R: People who see me now will not see me anymore. \q You will look for me, but I will be gone.

es.L: El ojo de [quien] me ve no me verá [más]; \q {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos [estarán] sobre mí, pero yo no [existiré].
es.B: El ojo que ahora me ve no me verá más; \q {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos me buscarán, pero ya no estaré.
es.R: Los que ahora me ven no me verán más. \q Me buscarás, pero ya no estaré.

fr.L: L’œil de [celui qui] me voit ne me verra [plus] ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux [seront] sur moi, mais je ne [serai] plus.
fr.B: L’œil qui me voit maintenant ne me verra plus ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux me chercheront, mais je ne serai plus là.
fr.R: Ceux qui me voient maintenant ne me verront plus. \q Tu me chercheras, mais je ne serai plus là.

sw.L: Jicho la [yule] anayeniona halitaniona [tena]; \q macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [yatakuwa] juu yangu, lakini mimi sitakuwako.
sw.B: Jicho linaloniona sasa halitaniona tena; \q macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yatanitafuta, lakini nitakuwa nimetoweka.
sw.R: Watu wanaoniona sasa hawataniona tena. \q Utanitafuta, lakini nitakuwa nimeondoka.

vi.L: Mắt của [người] thấy con sẽ không thấy con [nữa]; \q mắt Chúa [sẽ] nhìn con, nhưng con [sẽ] không còn.
vi.B: Mắt đang nhìn con sẽ không còn thấy con nữa; \q mắt Chúa sẽ tìm con, nhưng con đã không còn.
vi.R: Những người đang thấy con sẽ không thấy con nữa. \q Chúa sẽ tìm con, nhưng con đã đi rồi.

ko.L: 저를 보는 자의 눈이 [다시는] 저를 보지 못할 것이요, \q 주님의 눈이 저를 [찾으셔도] 저는 없을 것입니다.
ko.B: 지금 저를 보는 눈이 다시는 저를 보지 못하고, \q 주님께서 저를 찾으셔도 저는 이미 없을 것입니다.
ko.R: 지금 저를 보는 사람들도 다시는 저를 보지 못할 것입니다. \q 주님께서 저를 찾으셔도 저는 사라지고 없을 것입니다.

decisions.choice: the eye of one who sees me: anyone who looks at me now
decisions.reason: The phrase is "the eye of my seer": whoever sees Job now will soon not see him at all.

decisions.choice: your eyes on me: God will look for Job
decisions.reason: The second line has no verb: "your eyes on me". Set against the first line, it means God will turn his eyes to look for Job and not find him. 7:21 ends the same way.

decisions.choice: and I am not: I will be dead
decisions.reason: "I am not" ('enenni) means to be gone, no longer alive (Genesis 5:24 "he was not"; Psalm 39:14). Job's speech ends with the same word in 7:21.

decisions.choice: will look for me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Hebrew leaves out, with the sense of looking for someone who is not there (m2).

source.text: כָּלָ֣ה עָ֭נָן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ כֵּ֥ן יוֹרֵ֥ד שְׁ֝א֗וֹל לֹ֣א יַעֲלֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A cloud fades and goes; so one going down [to] Sheol does not come up.

en.L: A cloud fades and goes away; \q so one who goes down [to] Sheol does not come up.
en.B: As a cloud fades and is gone, \q so whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up again.
en.R: A cloud fades away and is gone. \q In the same way, a person who goes down to the grave never comes back up.

es.L: La nube se desvanece y se va; \q así el que baja [al] Seol no sube.
es.B: Como la nube se desvanece y se va, \q así el que baja al lugar de los muertos no vuelve a subir.
es.R: Una nube se deshace y desaparece. \q Del mismo modo, el que baja al lugar de los muertos nunca vuelve a subir.

fr.L: La nuée se dissipe et s’en va ; \q ainsi celui qui descend [au] Shéol ne remonte pas.
fr.B: Comme la nuée se dissipe et disparaît, \q ainsi celui qui descend au séjour des morts n’en remonte plus.
fr.R: Un nuage se dissipe et disparaît. \q De la même façon, celui qui descend au séjour des morts n’en remonte jamais.

sw.L: Wingu hufifia na kwenda zake; \q vivyo hivyo ashukaye Kuzimu hapandi.
sw.B: Kama wingu lififiavyo na kutoweka, \q ndivyo ashukaye Kuzimu asivyopanda tena.
sw.R: Wingu hufifia na kutoweka. \q Vivyo hivyo, mtu anayeshuka Kuzimu harudi juu kamwe.

vi.L: Mây tan đi và qua mất; \q cũng vậy kẻ xuống Âm Phủ không trở lên.
vi.B: Như mây tan biến rồi mất đi, \q người xuống Âm Phủ cũng chẳng trở lên.
vi.R: Đám mây tan đi rồi biến mất. \q Cũng vậy, người đã xuống nơi của người chết không bao giờ trở lên.

ko.L: 구름이 사라져 가듯이, \q 스올로 내려가는 자는 올라오지 못합니다.
ko.B: 구름이 사라져 없어지듯이, \q 스올로 내려간 사람은 다시 올라오지 못합니다.
ko.R: 구름이 흩어져 사라지듯이, \q 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳으로 내려간 사람은 다시는 올라오지 못합니다.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the world of the dead, pictured as below the earth, where everyone goes at death (3:13-19; 17:13-16). It is not a place of punishment in this book.

decisions.choice: does not come up: does not return to life on earth
decisions.reason: Job is speaking of return to this life, as the next verse shows (he does not come back to his house). The question of life after death comes up again in 14:7-14, where Job wonders whether a man who dies will live again.

decisions.choice: a cloud that fades: a picture of what passes and is gone
decisions.reason: A cloud melts away in the heat of the sun and leaves nothing behind (Hosea 6:4; 13:3).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Sheol"; Readable says "the grave", the book's choice for this word.

decisions.choice: "le séjour des morts" at Balanced and Readable, "le Shéol" at Literal
alternatives: "la tombe" at Readable, as the English
decisions.reason: The book's terms note keeps "le séjour des morts" for Sheol at Balanced and Readable, as in Psalms, though the English Readable says "the grave": French "la tombe" is one grave, not the place of all the dead (m1).

source.text: לֹא־יָשׁ֣וּב ע֣וֹד לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹא־יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He will not return again to his house, and not will recognize him again his place.

en.L: He will not return again to his house, \q and his place will not know him again.
en.B: He will never return to his home again, \q and his place will know him no more.
en.R: That person never comes home again, \q and the place where they lived forgets them.

es.L: No volverá más a su casa, \q y su lugar no lo conocerá más.
es.B: Nunca más volverá a su hogar, \q y su lugar no lo conocerá más.
es.R: Esa persona nunca vuelve a casa, \q y el lugar donde vivía la olvida.

fr.L: Il ne retournera plus à sa maison, \q et son lieu ne le connaîtra plus.
fr.B: Il ne reviendra plus jamais chez lui, \q et le lieu où il était ne le connaîtra plus.
fr.R: Celui-là ne revient jamais chez lui, \q et l’endroit où il vivait l’oublie.

sw.L: Hatarudi tena nyumbani kwake, \q wala mahali pake hapatamjua tena.
sw.B: Hatarudi kamwe nyumbani kwake tena, \q wala mahali pake hapatamtambua tena.
sw.R: Mtu huyo harudi nyumbani tena kamwe, \q na mahali alipoishi panamsahau.

vi.L: Người sẽ không trở về nhà mình nữa, \q và chỗ ở của người sẽ chẳng biết người nữa.
vi.B: Người ấy sẽ không bao giờ trở về nhà nữa, \q và nơi người ở sẽ chẳng còn biết đến người.
vi.R: Người ấy không bao giờ về nhà nữa, \q và nơi người ấy từng sống cũng quên người ấy đi.

ko.L: 그는 다시 자기 집으로 돌아오지 못하고, \q 그의 처소도 그를 다시 알지 못합니다.
ko.B: 그는 다시는 자기 집에 돌아오지 못하고, \q 그가 살던 곳도 그를 더 이상 알아보지 못합니다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 다시는 집에 돌아오지 못하고, \q 그가 살던 곳도 그를 잊어버립니다.

decisions.choice: his place will not know him: he is gone and forgotten
decisions.reason: The same saying is in Psalm 103:16. The place where a person lived no longer "recognizes" him: he is absent, and in time no one remembers him there.

decisions.choice: his house: his home and household
decisions.reason: The house (bayit) is both the building and the family in it. The dead do not come back to either.

decisions.choice: he ... his
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the singular of the Hebrew, which means anyone who dies (7:9) and Job above all. Readable says "that person" and "they", which keeps the general sense.

source.text: גַּם־אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Also I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

en.L: As for me, I will not hold back my mouth; \q I will speak in the distress of my spirit; \q I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
en.B: So I will not keep silent; \q I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit; \q I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
en.R: So I will not keep quiet. \q I will speak out of the pain in my spirit \q and complain out of the bitterness I feel inside.

es.L: Yo, pues, no refrenaré mi boca; \q hablaré en la angustia de mi espíritu; \q me quejaré en la amargura de mi alma.
es.B: Por eso no me callaré; \q hablaré en la angustia de mi espíritu, \q me quejaré en la amargura de mi alma.
es.R: Así que no me voy a callar. \q Hablaré desde el dolor que hay en mi espíritu \q y me quejaré de la amargura que siento por dentro.

fr.L: Moi donc, je ne retiendrai pas ma bouche ; \q je parlerai dans la détresse de mon esprit ; \q je me plaindrai dans l’amertume de mon âme.
fr.B: Je ne me tairai donc pas ; \q je parlerai dans l’angoisse de mon esprit, \q je me plaindrai dans l’amertume de mon âme.
fr.R: Alors je ne vais pas me taire. \q Je parlerai de la douleur qui est dans mon esprit \q et je me plaindrai de l’amertume que je ressens au fond de moi.

sw.L: Basi mimi sitakizuia kinywa changu; \q nitanena katika dhiki ya roho yangu; \q nitalalamika katika uchungu wa nafsi yangu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo sitanyamaza; \q nitasema katika dhiki ya roho yangu, \q nitalalamika katika uchungu wa nafsi yangu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sitakaa kimya. \q Nitasema kutokana na maumivu ya roho yangu \q na kulalamika kutokana na uchungu nilio nao moyoni.

vi.L: Phần con, con sẽ chẳng giữ miệng mình; \q con sẽ nói trong nỗi khổ của tâm linh con; \q con sẽ than thở trong sự cay đắng của linh hồn con.
vi.B: Vậy con sẽ không im lặng; \q con sẽ nói ra trong nỗi đau đớn của tâm linh, \q con sẽ than van trong cay đắng của linh hồn.
vi.R: Vậy con sẽ không im lặng nữa. \q Con sẽ nói ra nỗi đau trong tâm linh con \q và than thở về nỗi cay đắng trong lòng con.

ko.L: 그러므로 저도 제 입을 막지 않겠습니다. \q 제 영의 괴로움 속에서 말하고, \q 제 영혼의 쓰라림 속에서 탄식하겠습니다.
ko.B: 그러니 저는 잠잠히 있지 않겠습니다. \q 제 영의 고통 속에서 말하고, \q 제 영혼의 쓰라림 속에서 하소연하겠습니다.
ko.R: 그래서 저는 입을 다물고 있지 않겠습니다. \q 제 마음속 아픔을 털어놓고, \q 속에서 느끼는 쓰라림을 하소연하겠습니다.

decisions.choice: as for me: Job's answer to the shortness of life
decisions.reason: "Also I" (gam 'ani) is emphatic. Since his life is a breath and death is near (7:7-10), Job will not keep quiet: he will say what he feels while he can.

decisions.choice: spirit and soul: Job's inner self
decisions.reason: Spirit (ruach) and soul (nefesh) stand side by side for the whole inner person. "Bitterness of soul" is deep grief (1 Samuel 1:10; Job 10:1).

decisions.choice: complain: pour out one's troubled thoughts
decisions.reason: The verb (siach) means to muse or talk over something, and in distress to lament or complain (Psalm 142:3). The noun comes again in 7:13.

decisions.choice: I will not keep silent
alternatives: I will not restrain my mouth
decisions.reason: "Restrain my mouth" means to keep from speaking; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: הֲֽיָם־אָ֭נִי אִם־תַּנִּ֑ין כִּֽי־תָשִׂ֖ים עָלַ֣י מִשְׁמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Am] I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set over me a guard?

en.L: [Am] I the sea, or a sea monster, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set a guard over me?
en.B: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put me under guard?
en.R: Am I the sea, or some monster from the sea, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} must keep me under guard?

es.L: ¿[Soy] yo el mar, o un monstruo marino, \q para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pongas guardia sobre mí?
es.B: ¿Soy yo el mar, o el monstruo del abismo, \q para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me tengas bajo guardia?
es.R: ¿Soy yo el mar, o algún monstruo del mar, \q para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} tengas que vigilarme?

fr.L: Est-ce que je [suis] la mer, ou un monstre marin, \q pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mettes une garde sur moi ?
fr.B: Suis-je la mer ou le monstre des abîmes, \q pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me tiennes sous bonne garde ?

decisions.choice: the sea and the sea monster: powers God holds in check
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament's poetry the sea and its monsters stand for wild powers that God alone controls and keeps within bounds (Job 38:8-11; Psalm 74:13; Isaiah 51:9). Job asks bitterly whether he is such a threat that God must keep watch over him.

decisions.choice: sea monster: a great creature of the sea
decisions.reason: The word (tannin) is used of the great sea creatures God made (Genesis 1:21) and, in poetry, of a monster of the deep (Isaiah 27:1). Here it stands beside the sea as its creature.

decisions.choice: a guard: a watch set over someone
decisions.reason: The word (mishmar) is a guard or place of custody (Genesis 40:3). God keeps Job under constant watch; 7:17-20 says the same.

decisions.choice: you, with "You" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Job is speaking to God (7:7), so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for "you" in the middle of Job's sentences to God, with "Chúa" as the word of address
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms, Vietnamese speaks to God as "Ngài" or "Chúa"; where the English spans "you" mid-sentence the Vietnamese "Ngài" carries the same setting, while "Chúa", a noun of address, takes none.

decisions.choice: shatter: break down with fear
decisions.reason: The verb (chatat) means to be shattered, broken in spirit by fear (Jeremiah 1:17). God, Job says, sends the dreams that rob him of rest.

decisions.choice: dreams and visions
decisions.reason: Eliphaz had told of a vision in the night that made his bones shake (4:12-16), and used it to rebuke Job. Job's night visions bring him only terror, and he says God sends them.

decisions.choice: and: then, in answer to verse 13
decisions.reason: The "and" here gives the result of verse 13: when Job hopes for rest, God frightens him instead. The sentence runs on into verse 15.

decisions.choice: nightmares
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of dreams they are: dreams that terrify are nightmares.

decisions.choice: strangling: choking to death
decisions.reason: The word (machanaq) appears only here; it comes from the verb used of strangling (2 Samuel 17:23, Ahithophel; Nahum 2:13). Job would rather choke to death than go on as he is.

decisions.choice: my bones: this wasted body
decisions.reason: "Bones" stands for the body, and for Job's body reduced to skin and bone (19:20). Some suggest the Hebrew once read "my pains", a word of similar letters; the text as it stands makes good sense.

decisions.choice: my soul: I myself
decisions.reason: Soul (nefesh) here means the self, with its longing and choosing: "I would choose".

decisions.choice: this body of mine
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "bones" stands for (m2); Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: I loathe [my life]: the object is understood
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'as) has no object. Job says the same with the object in 9:21 ("I loathe my life") and 10:1, so it is supplied here.

decisions.choice: I would not live forever
decisions.reason: The words "I will not live forever" can state a fact or a wish. Next to "I loathe my life" they most likely say Job does not want his life drawn out. Either way he asks God to leave him alone for the little time he has.

decisions.choice: a breath: brief and without weight
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is a breath or vapor, the key word of Ecclesiastes (Ecclesiastes 1:2). It echoes 7:7: life is soon gone.

decisions.choice: cease from me: let me alone
decisions.reason: "Cease from me" asks God to stop dealing with Job, to leave him in peace (10:20; 14:6).

decisions.choice: I loathe [my life]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves out (m1).

decisions.choice: What is humankind: words from Psalm 8:5
decisions.reason: Job takes up the question of Psalm 8:5 ("What is humankind that you remember him?"). The psalm marvels that God cares for frail humans; Job turns it round and complains that God will not stop watching him.

decisions.choice: make him great: treat him as important
decisions.reason: The verb (gadal, intensive form) means to make great or to think much of. Here it is ironic: God takes so much notice of a mere human that he will not leave him alone.

decisions.choice: set your heart on: pay attention to
decisions.reason: To set the heart on someone is to give them close attention. God used the same words of Job in 1:8 and 2:3 ("Have you set your heart on my servant Job?"); now Job wishes God would not.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording, with "man ... him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) means any human being, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default. Readable's "human beings" is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: pay attention to / keep your mind on
decisions.reason: The heart in Hebrew is the seat of thought and attention; Balanced and Readable say so (m3).

decisions.choice: "사람이 무엇이기에 주님께서 ..." closing verse 17 as its own question
decisions.reason: Korean keeps the opening words of the published Korean Psalm 8:5 so the echo Job turns against God (m1) is heard, and closes the verse with its verb; verse 18 asks its own question.

fr.R: Tu les surveilles chaque matin \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les mets à l’épreuve à chaque instant.

sw.L: na kumjilia kila asubuhi, \q kila dakika kumjaribu?
sw.B: hata uwakague kila asubuhi \q na kuwajaribu kila dakika?
sw.R: Unawakagua kila asubuhi \q na kuwajaribu kila wakati.

vi.L: và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thăm viếng họ mỗi buổi sáng, \q mỗi giây phút {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thử thách họ?
vi.B: mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xem xét họ mỗi buổi sáng \q và thử thách họ từng giây phút?
vi.R: Ngài dò xét họ mỗi buổi sáng \q và thử thách họ từng lúc.

ko.L: 아침마다 그를 찾아오시고, \q 순간마다 그를 시험하십니까?
ko.B: 아침마다 그를 살피시고 \q 순간마다 그를 시험하십니까?
ko.R: 주님께서는 아침마다 사람을 살피시고 \q 순간마다 시험하십니다.

decisions.choice: visit: inspect, call to account
decisions.reason: The verb (paqad) means to look into, to inspect, and so either to care for or to call to account. Next to "test" it is close examination that Job finds unbearable.

decisions.choice: test: examine closely
decisions.reason: The verb (bachan) is used for testing metal (Zechariah 13:9) and for God examining the heart (Psalm 139:23). Job feels he is never out of God's sight.

decisions.choice: to mornings, to moments: every morning, all the time
decisions.reason: The plurals with "to" mean each morning and each moment: without a break.

decisions.choice: them, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to humankind (7:17), so it takes the gender setting.

source.text: כַּ֭מָּה לֹא־תִשְׁעֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי לֹֽא־תַ֝רְפֵּ֗נִי עַד־בִּלְעִ֥י רֻקִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: How long will you not look away from me, not let me alone until I swallow my spit?

en.L: How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not look away from me, \q [and] not let me alone until I swallow my spit?
en.B: How long before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look away from me \q and let me alone long enough to swallow my spit?
en.R: Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} never look away from me? \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not leave me alone even for a moment?

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo no apartarás [la vista] de mí, \q [ni] me dejarás hasta que trague mi saliva?
es.B: ¿Cuánto falta para que apartes la vista de mí \q y me dejes en paz siquiera para tragar saliva?
es.R: ¿Nunca vas a dejar de mirarme? \q ¿No me dejarás en paz ni por un momento?

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand ne détourneras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas de moi [ton regard], \q [et] ne me laisseras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas jusqu’à ce que j’avale ma salive ?
fr.B: Combien de temps encore avant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détournes de moi {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} regard \q et me laisses le temps d’avaler ma salive ?
fr.R: Ne vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} jamais cesser de me regarder ? \q Ne me laisseras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas tranquille ne serait-ce qu’un instant ?

sw.L: Hata lini hutaniondolea macho, \q [wala] hutaniacha hata nimeze mate yangu?
sw.B: Itakuwa hadi lini ndipo uache kunitazama, \q na kuniacha walau nimeze mate yangu?
sw.R: Je, hutaacha kamwe kunitazama? \q Je, hutaniacha hata kwa kitambo kidogo?

vi.L: Cho đến bao giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mới thôi nhìn con, \q [và] để con yên cho đến khi con nuốt nước bọt?
vi.B: Đến bao giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mới quay mắt khỏi con, \q để con yên dù chỉ đủ nuốt nước bọt?
vi.R: Chẳng lẽ Chúa không bao giờ thôi nhìn con sao? \q Chúa không để con yên dù chỉ một chút sao?

ko.L: 언제까지 제게서 눈을 돌리지 않으시며, \q 제가 침을 삼킬 동안도 저를 놓아두지 않으시겠습니까?
ko.B: 언제쯤 제게서 눈을 돌리시고, \q 침이라도 삼킬 만큼 저를 놓아두시겠습니까?
ko.R: 주님께서는 제게서 눈을 떼지 않으시렵니까? \q 잠시도 저를 내버려 두지 않으시렵니까?

decisions.choice: until I swallow my spit: for the shortest moment
decisions.reason: "Until I swallow my spit" is a saying for a very short time. Job asks for the briefest break from God's watching.

decisions.choice: look away from me: stop watching me
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'ah) with "from" means to turn one's gaze away. Job asks the same in 14:6: "Look away from him, so that he may rest."

decisions.choice: how long: an impatient question
decisions.reason: "How long" (kammah) asks when God will stop, with the sense that it has gone on too long.

decisions.choice: even for a moment
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the saying (m1) rather than the picture.

source.text: חָטָ֡אתִי מָ֤ה אֶפְעַ֨ל׀לָךְ֮ נֹצֵ֪ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם לָ֤מָה שַׂמְתַּ֣נִי לְמִפְגָּ֣ע לָ֑ךְ וָאֶהְיֶ֖ה עָלַ֣י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: I have sinned; what do I do to you, watcher of humankind? Why have you set me as a target for you, and I am on myself a burden?

en.L: [If] I have sinned, what do I do to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q watcher of humankind? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set me as a target for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, \q so that I am a burden to myself?
en.B: If I have sinned, what harm have I done to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q watcher of humankind? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} target, \q so that I have become a burden to myself?
en.R: Suppose I have sinned. What harm does that do to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep such close watch on people? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} target? \q Why have I become a burden to myself?

es.L: [Si] he pecado, ¿qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hago, \q guardián de la humanidad? \q ¿Por qué me has puesto como blanco para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q de modo que soy una carga para mí mismo?
es.B: Si he pecado, ¿qué daño {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} he hecho, \q vigilante de la humanidad? \q ¿Por qué me has hecho {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} blanco, \q hasta el punto de ser una carga para mí mismo?
es.R: Supongamos que he pecado. ¿Qué daño {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hace eso, \q si {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} vigilas tan de cerca a la gente? \q ¿Por qué me has hecho {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} blanco? \q ¿Por qué me he vuelto una carga para mí mismo?

fr.L: [Si] j’ai péché, que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fais-je, \q gardien des humains ? \q Pourquoi m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} établi comme cible pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q en sorte que je suis un fardeau pour moi-même ?
fr.B: Si j’ai péché, quel mal {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai-je fait, \q gardien des humains ? \q Pourquoi as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fait de moi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cible, \q au point que je suis devenu un fardeau pour moi-même ?
fr.R: Supposons que j’aie péché. Quel mal cela {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fait-il, \q {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui surveilles de si près les gens ? \q Pourquoi as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fait de moi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cible ? \q Pourquoi suis-je devenu un fardeau pour moi-même ?

sw.L: [Kama] nimetenda dhambi, nakufanyia nini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q mlinzi wa wanadamu? \q Kwa nini umeniweka kuwa shabaha kwa ajili yako {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, \q hata nimekuwa mzigo kwangu mwenyewe?
sw.B: Kama nimetenda dhambi, nimekudhuru nini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q mlinzi wa wanadamu? \q Kwa nini umenifanya shabaha {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, \q hata nimekuwa mzigo kwangu mwenyewe?
sw.R: Tuseme nimetenda dhambi. Hilo linakudhuru nini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q kwa kuwa unawachunguza watu kwa karibu hivyo? \q Kwa nini umenifanya shabaha {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}? \q Kwa nini nimekuwa mzigo kwangu mwenyewe?

vi.L: [Nếu] con đã phạm tội, thì con làm gì đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q hỡi Đấng canh chừng loài người? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt con làm cái đích cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q đến nỗi con thành gánh nặng cho chính mình?
vi.B: Nếu con có phạm tội, thì con đã làm hại gì đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q hỡi Đấng canh giữ loài người? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy con làm đích nhắm, \q đến nỗi con trở thành gánh nặng cho chính mình?
vi.R: Cứ cho là con đã phạm tội. Điều đó có hại gì cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} theo dõi loài người sát sao như thế? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy con làm đích nhắm? \q Sao con lại thành gánh nặng cho chính mình?

ko.L: [만일] 제가 죄를 지었다 한들, \q 사람을 지켜보시는 분이시여, 제가 주님께 무엇을 하였습니까? \q 어찌하여 저를 주님의 과녁으로 삼으셔서 \q 제가 저 자신에게 짐이 되게 하셨습니까?
ko.B: 제가 죄를 지었다 해도, \q 사람을 감시하시는 분이시여, 그것이 주님께 무슨 해가 됩니까? \q 어찌하여 저를 주님의 과녁으로 삼으셔서 \q 제가 저 자신에게도 짐이 되게 하셨습니까?
ko.R: 제가 죄를 지었다고 치더라도, \q 사람을 그토록 가까이 지켜보시는 주님께 그것이 무슨 해가 되겠습니까? \q 어찌하여 저를 과녁으로 삼으셨습니까? \q 어찌하여 제가 저 자신에게 짐이 되었습니까?

decisions.choice: I have sinned: if I have sinned
decisions.reason: Job does not confess here; he grants a sin for the sake of argument. Hebrew can state a condition without "if" (as 10:14; 35:6). Even if he has sinned, he asks, what harm can a mortal do to God?

decisions.choice: watcher of humankind: one who watches people closely
decisions.reason: The verb behind "watcher" (natsar) often means to guard and protect (Psalm 12:8). Here, after the guard of 7:12 and the testing of 7:18, it is bitter: God keeps watch on Job to catch him.

decisions.choice: a target: something to strike at
decisions.reason: The word (mifga') comes from the verb "to strike, to meet". Job feels God has made him the mark for his arrows (6:4; 16:12).

decisions.choice: a burden to myself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "to myself". Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among the places where the scribes are said to have changed a phrase out of reverence, from "to you" (to God); the old Greek translation also reads "to you". Read that way, Job asks why he has become a burden to God. The Hebrew as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: [If]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the "if" that the sense needs (m1); Balanced and Readable give it without brackets.

decisions.choice: since you keep such close watch on people
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title into a clause so that its bitter sense (m2) is clear.

source.text: וּמֶ֤ה׀לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֪יר אֶת־עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And why will you not forgive my transgression and take away my iniquity? For now in [the] dust I will lie down, and you will seek me, and I [am] not.

en.L: And why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not pardon my transgression \q and take away my iniquity? \q For now I will lie down in the dust; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will search for me, but I [will be] no more.
en.B: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not pardon my offense \q and take away my guilt? \q For soon I will lie down in the dust; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will look for me, but I will be gone.
en.R: Why will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not forgive me for the wrong I have done \q and take away my sin? \q Soon I will lie down in the dust of the grave. \q You will look for me, but I will be gone.

es.L: ¿Y por qué no perdonas mi transgresión \q ni quitas mi iniquidad? \q Porque ahora me acostaré en el polvo; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me buscarás, pero yo no [existiré].
es.B: ¿Por qué no perdonas mi ofensa \q y quitas mi culpa? \q Porque pronto me acostaré en el polvo; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me buscarás, pero ya no estaré.
es.R: ¿Por qué no me perdonas el mal que he hecho \q y quitas mi pecado? \q Pronto me acostaré en el polvo de la tumba. \q Me buscarás, pero ya no estaré.

fr.L: Et pourquoi ne pardonnes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas ma transgression \q et n’ôtes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas mon iniquité ? \q Car maintenant je vais me coucher dans la poussière ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me chercheras, mais je ne [serai] plus.
fr.B: Pourquoi ne pardonnes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas ma faute \q et n’enlèves-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas ma culpabilité ? \q Car bientôt je me coucherai dans la poussière ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me chercheras, mais je ne serai plus là.
fr.R: Pourquoi ne veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas me pardonner le mal que j’ai fait \q et effacer mon péché ? \q Bientôt je me coucherai dans la poussière de la tombe. \q Tu me chercheras, mais je ne serai plus là.

sw.L: Na kwa nini husamehi kosa langu \q wala kuuondoa uovu wangu? \q Kwa maana sasa nitalala mavumbini; \q utanitafuta, lakini mimi sitakuwako.
sw.B: Kwa nini husamehi kosa langu \q na kuiondoa hatia yangu? \q Kwa maana punde nitalala mavumbini; \q utanitafuta, lakini nitakuwa nimetoweka.
sw.R: Kwa nini hunisamehi kwa ubaya niliotenda \q na kuiondoa dhambi yangu? \q Punde nitalala katika mavumbi ya kaburi. \q Utanitafuta, lakini nitakuwa nimeondoka.

vi.L: Và sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không tha sự vi phạm của con \q và cất đi tội ác của con? \q Vì bây giờ con sẽ nằm trong bụi đất; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ tìm con, nhưng con [sẽ] không còn.
vi.B: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không tha lỗi cho con \q và cất bỏ tội của con? \q Vì chẳng bao lâu con sẽ nằm trong bụi đất; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ tìm con, nhưng con đã không còn.
vi.R: Sao Chúa không tha thứ điều sai con đã làm \q và cất tội lỗi con đi? \q Chẳng bao lâu nữa con sẽ nằm trong bụi đất nơi mồ mả. \q Chúa sẽ tìm con, nhưng con đã đi rồi.

ko.L: 어찌하여 제 허물을 용서하지 않으시며, \q 제 죄악을 없애 주지 않으십니까? \q 이제 제가 티끌 속에 누울 것이니, \q 주님께서 저를 찾으셔도 저는 없을 것입니다.
ko.B: 어찌하여 제 잘못을 용서하지 않으시고 \q 제 죄를 없애 주지 않으십니까? \q 저는 곧 티끌 속에 누울 것입니다. \q 주님께서 저를 찾으셔도 저는 이미 없을 것입니다.
ko.R: 어찌하여 제가 저지른 잘못을 용서하지 않으시고 \q 제 죄를 없애 주지 않으십니까? \q 저는 곧 무덤의 흙 속에 눕게 될 것입니다. \q 주님께서 저를 찾으셔도 저는 사라지고 없을 것입니다.

decisions.choice: forgive: lift away
decisions.reason: The verb (nasa') means to lift or carry; with sin as its object it means to forgive, to take the sin away (Exodus 34:7; Psalm 32:5).

decisions.choice: transgression and iniquity: wrongs and their guilt
decisions.reason: Transgression (pesha') is a breach of faith, a rebellion; iniquity ('awon) is wrongdoing and the guilt it brings. Together they cover whatever Job may have done (7:20).

decisions.choice: lie down in the dust: die and be buried
decisions.reason: To lie down in the dust is to die and return to the dust (Genesis 3:19; Job 20:11; 21:26).

decisions.choice: you will seek me: look for me eagerly
decisions.reason: The verb (shachar) means to look for earnestly; it may be linked with the word for dawn, "to seek early". Job pictures God looking for him at last, perhaps to show him favor, and finding him gone, as in 7:8. Bildad uses the same verb in 8:5.

decisions.choice: soon
decisions.reason: "Now" here means that death is close; Balanced and Readable say "soon".

decisions.choice: offense ... guilt
decisions.reason: Balanced uses everyday words for the pair (m2); Literal keeps the traditional terms.
